wheel.offset: ET20–35 range by body (no single factory figure)
wheel.lug_torque: 130 N·m (96 lb-ft) for alloy wheels and 108 N·m (80 lb-ft) for steel wheels (Haynes); a 1993 NAS 110 V8 data set also gives 130 N·m, and one other data set gives 170 N·m

max_tire.note: The popular upgrade. Owners report rub on the front radius arms at full lock (wind out the steering stops), against the 45 L auxiliary tank on 110s, and close to the spring brackets at full compression.
A 110 owner on 2 in, no spacers, reports light rub on the radius arms at full lock. 295/85R16 is a taller, narrower option with little tread choice.

AULRO owners needed 2–3 in of lift plus extended flares or trimming, offset wheels (8–10 in wide), extended bump stops, castor correction, stronger halfshafts/CVs and lower gearing. A Tdi will feel gutless.

items.title: Driveshaft nuts replaced with wrong size at port of entry
items.summary: A port-of-entry pinion-torque check meant removing the driveshafts, and they went back on with the wrong nuts. 155 Defenders, Discoveries and County Classics were covered.

items.title: Battery hazardous-substance warning label missing
items.summary: The required hazard label wasn't fitted to the battery; 4,254 Defenders covered.

tsbs.title: 300Tdi timing-belt modification kit
tsbs.summary: Early 300Tdi setups could let the belt track off. The revised kit (sold as STC4096L-type) adds a flanged crank pulley and spaced idler; ask for proof it's fitted.

tsbs.title: Td5 oil wicking into the injector loom
tsbs.summary: Oil migrates through the injector harness toward the ECU; check the barrel connector between engine and injector looms.

identify.intro: Defenders get cloned, re-dated and dressed up as NAS trucks, and a gray-market import with a mismatched VIN can be seized. Check the numbers before you check the paint.

items.head: VIN plate and chassis stamp
items.body: The VIN plate sits on the bulkhead or brake servo under the bonnet; match it to the number stamped on the front chassis rail and the title. For an import, the build date must really be 25+ years old.

items.head: Rest-of-world VIN
items.body: Ninety/One Ten VINs start SALLD. Position 6 is V for Ninety or H for One Ten; position 7 is body (A regular, B Ninety Station Wagon, H High Capacity Pickup, M One Ten Station Wagon); position 8 is engine (B 2.5 TD, C 2.5 D, D 2.5 petrol, F 2.5 Tdi, G 2.25 D, H 2.25 petrol, V V8).

items.head: Genuine NAS trucks
items.body: NAS Defenders carry a US-format 17-character VIN (RM Sotheby's examples: SALDV2285RA941249 for a 1994 D90, SALDV2246VA118787 for a 1997), a numbered NAS badge, a full external roll cage, larger side indicators and taillights, factory air and four-wheel discs. All have the 3.9 or 4.0 V8.

items.head: 200Tdi or 300Tdi?
items.body: The 200Tdi has two V-belts and a big aluminium block-to-sump strengthener; the 300Tdi has a single serpentine belt, no strengthener, a smaller water pump mounted higher and a piston-type vacuum pump.

items.head: Heritage certificate
items.body: The British Motor Museum's Heritage Certificate copies the factory ledger entry (build and despatch dates, engine number, colour, equipment) and covers Land Rovers from 1948 on. Useful for proving a build date or NAS spec.

capability.note: 750 kg unbraked; 2004 90/110/130 per CarsGuide, same figures for a 2009 90 per GoAuto
1993 Defender 110 V8; a 2009 Defender 90 is listed at 60 L
ECD's estimates (method not stated); V8 12–14 in real-world use

values.intro: NAS trucks carry a big premium over gray-market imports, and original, documented 1993 110s are the top of the market; Tdi imports are the affordable way in.
values.note: Based on Bring a Trailer sold results in 2025–26: 14 NAS D90s ($40,000–106,000, median about $59,000), three 1993 NAS 110s ($62,500–135,000), 10 Euro 90s and 9 Euro 110s ($17,250–69,003, apart from two LS3-swapped 90s at $61,000 and $145,500). Atlantic British puts the very best NAS 110s near $200,000.

paragraphs: Only the NAS trucks (1993 110, 1994–97 90) were sold new in the US, so every other classic Defender here is a gray-market import. NHTSA lets a vehicle in without meeting federal safety standards (FMVSS) once it is at least 25 years old, counted from its date of manufacture, declared under Box 1 on the HS-7. In October 2026 that means trucks built before October 2001: 200Tdi, 300Tdi, V8 and early Td5 Defenders. A newer Defender can't be made to comply, and Puma trucks (2007 on) won't start qualifying until 2032.

The EPA side is separate. On Form 3520-1, exemption code E covers vehicles at least 21 years old (calendar year of manufacture subtracted from year of import) in original, unmodified configuration. A truck with a replacement engine doesn't qualify unless it's the same engine model as original, so an engine-swapped Defender should be imported before the swap, not after.

Enforcement is real. In 2014 Homeland Security agents seized more than two dozen Defenders imported by one North Carolina owner on suspicion that VINs had been swapped to beat the 25-year rule; in 2015 they were found to have been correctly imported and ordered returned, after a pro bono legal challenge. Make sure the VIN plate, chassis stamp, title and build date agree before you pay, and a Heritage Certificate helps.

State rules come last and matter most in California. Its smog-check exemptions cover gasoline vehicles of the 1975 model year and older and diesels of the 1997 model year and older, but a direct import from 1975 on that was never certified for California is supposed to get a CARB Certificate of Conformance after a laboratory test, and ECD warns a classic Defender engine can keep the truck off California roads. Check with your DMV and, in California, with CARB before you buy.

production.intro: The Ninety/One Ten/Defender ran from 1983 to January 2016, and only a few thousand were sold new in North America.
